title: Rationalize SDK compatibility matrix and stage gradual API-surface deprecations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce long-term maintenance cost and customer confusion by producing a single, vetted compatibility matrix for Python/JS/Go SDKs, performing coordinated minor dependency bumps, and staging API-surface deprecations with automated migration guidance and telemetry.

Scope:
- Audit runtime- and transport-related dependencies across all three language clients (requests/urllib3, node-fetch/undici, golang http client and go modules).
- Identify safe minor/patch bumps and a small set of breaking changes we will deprecate (legacy auth helpers, old response wrappers, deprecated request params).
- Add cross-language compatibility tests that run against a pinned local runtime image and the hosted API to detect behavioral regressions.
- Create automated deprecation warnings surfaced in SDKs and in the Console usage analytics for early adopters.
- Publish migration guides, example PRs, and a rollout plan with canary percentages.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compatibility matrix doc published and approved by SDK leads.
- CI job added that runs cross-language smoke tests on every client PR and nightly matrix permutations.
- At least three minor dependency bumps merged per language (Python, JS, Go) without regressions in canary.
- Deprecation telemetry wired to console-usage (counts of calls using deprecated params).
- Migration guide + code samples merged to docs and linked in SDK README.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge compatibility matrix and CI jobs (week 1).
2) Execute safe dependency bumps in a single coordinated release window; enable canary clients for 5% of tenant traffic for 48 hours.
3) Monitor errors, latency, and token-cost regressions; auto-rollback criteria defined in the PRD.
4) Announce deprecations with a 90-day window; surface in SDK logs and Console.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Coordinated upgrades across languages increase release coordination overhead but reduce fragmentation long-term.
- Aggressive bumps risk subtle behavior changes (JSON encoding, retry backoffs); mitigated via cross-language tests and runtime smoke runs.

Related docs and artifacts:
- Compatibility matrix draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/SDK+Compatibility+Matrix
- Migration guide draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk-migrations/2026
